title: A body in a changing field: gradient seen, fall from rest, level dependence

key_results.statement: Class: every $C_f$, $Y$, $\varphi$ and every start of body and medium, any $\kappa$; fixed $\lambda$; status: exact first-order coefficient. The first-order term in $Y$ of the view of $\{b,c\}$, and of every schedule of readings on $b$ and $c$, depends on the field only through the real function $\gamma(s)=\langle\varphi\vert e^{iC_fs}Ye^{-iC_fs}\vert\varphi\rangle$ on $[0,\lambda]$: $V(\lambda)=e^{-iC_{br}\lambda}\{\rho_0-i\int_0^\lambda ds\,\gamma(s)[B(s),\rho_0]\}e^{iC_{br}\lambda}+O(\lVert Y\rVert^2)$.

Same class and status as (12.3): the generator $C_{m eff}(\lambda)=C_{br}+\gamma(\lambda)\,\hat x\otimes G\otimes\mathbb 1_c$ on $\mathcal H_b\otimes\mathcal H_c$ reproduces the view and all schedules up to $O(\lVert YVert^2)$; it is the contract of an admissible description (A5) iff $\gamma$ is constant, i.e. $\hat\gamma_
u=0$ for all $
u
eq0$; for a sharp stationary field and for a field with (2.11) of 02-field-object, $\gamma$ is constant and the statement is exact at all orders.

Class: sharp start $Y\varphi=\gamma\varphi$ that is not stationary; expansion for $\lambda\to0$ at fixed operators; status: exact leading term. $1-\operatorname{Tr}V^2=\frac{\lambda^4}{2}\Gamma\lVert(Y-\gamma)C_f\varphi\rVert^2+O(\lambda^5)$, so the view first differs from the one of the generator at order $Y^2$ and $\lambda^4$ (at $\lambda^{2k_0+2}$ if (2.11) first fails at $k_0>1$; the $\lambda^4$ coefficient vanishes if $\Gamma=0$).

Class: every level and branch of Model D, every smooth $g$, every continuous $\gamma$; fixed start and fixed $\lambda$, $\kappa\to0$, $\langle X\rangle=0$; status: exact first-order coefficient. The first-order velocity of the mean position label is $v^{(1)}_g(\lambda)=\int_0^\lambda ds\,\gamma(s)\,\mathcal K_g(\lambda,s)$.

Same class and status as (12.6): $\mathcal K_g(\lambda,s)=\langle k_0+k_1\cos(2\omega(\lambda-s))\rangle_g-2\sigma M^2\int\frac{dp}{2\pi}\frac{\omega'}{\omega}\sin(2\omega(\lambda-s))[j_g+\sigma\lambda\omega'\lvert g\rvert^2]$ with $k_0=-M^2\omega''/\omega$, $k_1=-M^2\tau^2(M^2+\tau^2)\sin^2p/\omega^4$; it is an average $\langle\cdot\rangle_g$ of an explicit function only if $j_g=x_0\lvert g\rvert^2$; for a constant $\gamma$ it reproduces (4.7) of 04-branch-fall with $G_k=\gamma M_k$.

Class: every smooth $g$ at rest (exact bound), and the limit $\delta p\to0$ at fixed $\lambda$ for sequences of the class $\mathcal S_\chi$: $\lvert\mathcal K_g(\lambda,s)-K_{\chi_g}(\lambda-s)\rvert\le4\tau^2(1+\tau^2/M^2+\tau^2\lambda/M)(\delta p^2+2\rho_g)$ with the closed-form kernel $K_\chi(\Delta)=-\tau^2[1+\sigma\chi\sin(2M_k\Delta)]$.

Class $\mathcal S_\chi$, every level and branch, every continuous $\gamma$; limit $\delta p\to0$ at fixed $\lambda$; status: exact limits, velocity and acceleration each derived on its own. $v^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}(\lambda)=-\tau^2\int_0^\lambda ds\,\gamma(s)[1+\sigma\chi\sin(2M_k(\lambda-s))]$ and $a^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}(\lambda)=-\tau^2\gamma(\lambda)-2\sigma\chi M_k\tau^2\int_0^\lambda ds\,\gamma(s)\cos(2M_k(\lambda-s))$.

Class: every smooth $g$ at rest; fixed start and $\lambda$; status: exact bound for the acceleration itself. $\lvert a^{(1)}_g(\lambda)-a_{\chi_g}(\lambda)\rvert\le\tau^2\sup_{[0,\lambda]}\lvert\gamma\rvert(1+4M\lambda)(1+\tau^2/M^2+2\tau^2\lambda/M)(\delta p^2+2\rho_g)$.

Class $\mathcal S_\chi$, $\gamma=\gamma_0+\gamma_1\cos(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)$, $\Omega\neq2M_k$; limit $\delta p\to0$ at fixed $\lambda$; exact. The first-order velocity is the drift $-\tau^2\gamma_0\lambda$, plus a part of frequency $\Omega$ equal to $-\tau^2\gamma_1[\sin(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)/\Omega+\sigma\chi\,2M_k\cos(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)/(4M_k^2-\Omega^2)]$, plus a part of frequency $2M_k$ proportional to $\chi$, plus a constant.

Same class, order and status as (12.11): the first-order acceleration is $-\tau^2\gamma_0-\tau^2\gamma_1[\cos(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)-\sigma\chi\frac{2M_k\Omega}{4M_k^2-\Omega^2}\sin(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)]$ plus a part of frequency $2M_k$ proportional to $\chi$; no part grows with $\lambda$.

Class $\mathcal S_\chi$, $\Omega\neq2M_k$, limit $\delta p\to0$ at fixed $\lambda$, exact: $\mathcal A_{k,\sigma}(\Omega)=-\tau^2[1+i\sigma\chi\frac{2M_k\Omega}{4M_k^2-\Omega^2}]$; it tends to $-\tau^2$ for $\Omega\to0$, which is (4.16) of 04-branch-fall per unit gradient; for starts of one class on all levels it is the same for all levels iff $\chi=0$; its leading level dependence for $\Omega\ll2M_k$ is $-i\sigma\chi\tau^2\Omega/(2M_k)$.

Class $\mathcal S_\chi$, $\Omega=2M_k$, limit $\delta p\to0$ at fixed $\lambda$, exact: $v^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}(\lambda)=-\tau^2\gamma_0\lambda-\sigma\chi\tau^2\gamma_1\frac{\lambda}{2}\sin(2M_k\lambda+\vartheta)$ plus bounded terms; an oscillation of frequency $2M_k$ grows linearly in the level $k$ only, and not at all for $\chi=0$.

Class: every fixed smooth $g$, every $\Omega>0$; limit $\lambda\to\infty$ at a fixed start; status: leading order with rest $O(\lambda^{1/2})$. $v^{(1)}_g(\lambda)=\lambda\{\gamma_0\langle\alpha_0\rangle_g+\gamma_1\operatorname{Re}[c_g(\Omega)e^{i(\Omega\lambda+\vartheta)}]\}+o(\lambda)$ with $c_g(\Omega)=-\lim_{\epsilon\to0^+}\langle4M^2\omega'^2/(4\omega^2-(\Omega-i\epsilon)^2)\rangle_g$; then for $\delta p\to0$ at rest $c_g\to0$ for $\Omega<2M_k$ and $c_g\to-\tau^2$ for $\Omega=2M_k$ whatever $\chi$, so the two orders of limits do not commute at resonance.

Class $\mathcal S_\chi$, limit $\delta p\to0$ at fixed $\lambda$, exact (iff): $\lvert\mathcal A_{k,\sigma}(\Omega)+\tau^2\rvert\le\delta\tau^2$ for all levels iff $\Omega\notin\bigcup_k(\Omega^{(k)}_-,\Omega^{(k)}_+)$ with $\Omega^{(k)}_\mp=\frac{M_k}{\delta}(\sqrt{\chi^2+4\delta^2}\mp\lvert\chi\rvert)$; for a general $\gamma$ the acceleration from rest is $-\tau^2\gamma(\lambda)$ for all levels plus $\sigma\chi R_k[\gamma](\lambda)$.

Two-place field with $Y=y\lvert1\rangle\langle1\rvert$, $C_f=\gamma_f(\lvert0\rangle\langle1\rvert+\lvert1\rangle\langle0\rvert)$, $\varphi=\lvert0\rangle$: $\gamma(\lambda)=y\sin^2(\gamma_f\lambda)$, i.e. $\gamma_0=y/2$, $\gamma_1=-y/2$, $\Omega=2\lvert\gamma_f\rvert$; in the class $\mathcal S_0$ at fixed $\lambda$ the first-order acceleration is $-\tau^2y\sin^2(\gamma_f\lambda)$ for all levels; resonance at $\lvert\gamma_f\rvert=M_k$; controls: a sharp stationary field and a field with $[Y,C_f]=0$ give a constant $\gamma$.

open_issues: The level-dependent part of the response at fixed λ is carried entirely by the position-label correlation χ of the start, which grows under free motion; a formula uniform in λ between λ ≪ λ_g and λ ≫ λ_g is not derived, only the exact (12.6), (12.7) cover it.

Order (II) for a field frequency inside the band 2M_k < Ω ≤ 2√(M_k²+τ²): c_g(Ω) of (12.15) is defined for every start, but its limit δp → 0 is evaluated only for sequences that vanish near the labels with 2ω_k(p) = Ω.
Sequences of starts at rest with ρ_g not tending to 0 belong to no class S_χ; for them only (12.6), (12.7) and the bounds (12.8), (12.10) are available.
The growth at Ω = 2M_k is a statement on the first-order coefficient at each fixed λ; the range of λ in which it is the leading effect needs the second order in Y, which is outside the scope.

consistency_checks.check: Constant γ: (12.6), (12.7) reproduce the growing part of (4.7) of 04-branch-fall with G_k = γ M_k, and (12.9) at rest has the window average −τ²γ of (4.16).
Gradient pulse by an independent route (label shift by e^{−iεM x σ3}): the velocity response of a narrow start at rest equals ε K_χ(Δ) of (12.8), including the term proportional to χ.
Dimensions: velocities are costs, accelerations and kernels are costs squared, χ, γ and the purity deficit (12.5) are pure numbers.
